subject.title: Embedded agent: auto-rotate (or persist a marker) on context-overflow give_up instead of wedging the session until manual /reset

question: Should exhausted embedded-agent context-overflow recovery persist a durable blocked-overflow marker, auto-rotate and replay once, or keep manual recovery with better visibility?
rationale: The current code and docs intentionally preserve the session mapping and require manual `/reset` or `/new`; changing that affects core replay, session state, and operator recovery semantics.

options.title: Persist blocked state first
options.body: Add a durable overflow-blocked receipt and operator-visible recovery action without automatically replaying the pending turn on a new session.

options.title: Guarded one-shot rotation
options.body: Rotate and replay once after exhausted overflow recovery only with explicit replay-safety gates, loop caps, and tests for duplicate side effects.

options.title: Keep manual recovery
options.body: Retain documented `/reset` or `/new` recovery while improving diagnostics, docs, or UI visibility for blocked overflow sessions.

recommendation.title: Persist blocked state first
recommendation.body: Add a durable overflow-blocked receipt and operator-visible recovery action without automatically replaying the pending turn on a new session.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-schema and runtime ownership makes this the best available routing point for the durable-state versus auto-rotation decision.
